svg.title: 03 · Connection, on the user’s terms
svg.text: One shared starting point; Accept and Not now are alternative branches.
ILLUSTRATED REPLAY · DEMO / SCRIPTED · NOT SCREENSHOTS OR USER RESEARCH

svg.title: PawPal, a cream puppy with a lavender scarf, looking concerned

text.tspan: I feel lonely. I haven’t seen my friends in weeks.
That sounds lonely. Missing someone to share the little
parts of your day with can really ache. When has that
feeling been strongest lately?
A little connection, if you’d like
A short walk or a coffee with someone familiar. Only if
it feels right — there’s no hurry.
User sends a loneliness message.
Support first, then a clearly optional card.

svg.title: PawPal, a cream puppy with a lavender scarf, looking encouraging

text.tspan: Pick one person you feel comfortable with. You could
write: “Fancy a short walk or coffee this week?”
Nothing is sent. You decide whether and when.
Accept is a local choice, not a contact operation.
From panel 1, user selects Accept.
A small next step; nothing is sent.

svg.title: PawPal, a cream puppy with a lavender scarf, looking calm

text.tspan: Of course. Your pace. We can keep talking. I won’t
suggest another catch-up in this conversation unless
you ask.
Alternatively, user selects Not now in panel 1.
Refusal is respected for this conversation.

svg.title: PawPal, a cream puppy with a lavender scarf, looking concerned

text.tspan: I still feel lonely tonight.
It sounds like that lonely feeling is still there.
Quiet moments can make it feel more noticeable. We can
stay with how you feel, without rushing to do anything.
What is tonight like for you?
Proactive suggestions stay off unless the user asks again.
User continues talking about loneliness.
Emotional support continues; no new card.

svg.text: PawPal · same SVG character as the app · responses replayed from server/conversation.ts
Synthetic example student; no claim about emotional benefit or real-world social outcomes
